questions.question: National Youth Festival is celebrated on the birth anniversary of which of the following personalities?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Swami Vivekanand.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swami Vivekananda's birthday on January 12**__ is celebrated as National Youth Day and the week commencing from that day is known as the National Youth Week.
 
• The National Youth Festival in India is an annual gathering of youth with various activities including competitive ones.
 
• It is organized by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India in collaboration with one of the State Governments.
 
• Thus it is held in a different state each year during National Youth Week, 12 to 16 January every year.

questions.question: Which of the following Jyotirlingas is in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
Option **1** is correct:

__
 
• The **Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga**__ Temple is one of the ancient and holiest shrines of India.
 
• This temple is the holy abode of one of the **12 jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva**.
 
• The temple is located at a distance of 11km from **Daulatabad** near Aurangabad in Maharashtra. Daulatabad was once known as **Devagiri**.
 
• **Ahilyabhai Holkar** constructed the Grishneshwar Temple.
 
• **Grishneshwar** is also known as **Ghushmeswara**.
 
• Jyotirlinga are the 12 special shrines dedicated to Shiva since ancient times 
 
• These **12 jyotirlinga** shrines are:
 
 
• Somnath Jyotirling in Saurashtra (Gujarat),
 
• Mallikarjun jyotirlinga in Srisailam (Andhra Pradesh), 
 
• Mahakaleshwar jyotirlinga in Ujjain (Madya Pradesh),
 
• Omkareshwar jyotirlinga in Shivpuri / Samaleswari (Madhya Pradesh),
 
• Lord Baidyanath Jyotirlinga in Deoghar (Jharkhand),
 
• Nageswar jyotirlinga in Darukavanam (Gujarat)
 
• Kedareswar jyotirlinga in Kedarnath / Himalayas (Uttarakhand)
 
• Tryambakeswar jyotirlinga in Nasik (Maharashtra)
 
• Rameshwar jyotirlinga in Setubandanam / Rameshwaram (Tamil Nadu)
 
• Bhimashankar jyotirlinga in Dakini (Maharashtra)
 
• Visweswar jyotirlinga in Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh),
 
• Ghrishneswar jyotirlinga in Devasrovar (Maharashtra).

questions.question: India’s foreign reserves does NOT consist of which of the following?
questions.solution:
**__Answer : (2)__ - Carbon Bonds **

 
• The foreign exchange reserve of India consists of four categories- Foreign Currency Assets, Gold, Special Drawing Rights (SDR) and Reserve Tranche Position (RTP).
 
• SDR's are supplementary foreign exchange reserve assets defined and maintained by the International Monetary Fund (IMF). SDR's are the units of account for the IMF and not a currency. It was created in 1969 to supplement a shortfall of preferred foreign exchange reserve assets, namely gold and U.S. Dollars.
 
• Reserve Tranche Position (RTP) is the difference between the International Monetary Fund's holdings of that country's currency and the country's IMF designated quota.

questions.question: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution does NOT exercise its control to the tribal areas of which of the following state?
questions.solution:
Option** 2** is correct:

__
 
• The **Sixth Schedule** of the Indian Constitution provides for decentralized self-governance and dispute resolution in parts of the North East which are mainly tribal areas in the States of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram**.
 
• It is described in **Articles 244 and 275** of the Constitution.
 
• The **Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution** does NOT exercise its control to the tribal areas of **Manipur**__.

 
• Now the Constitution of India has 448 articles in 25 parts, 12 schedules.
 
• There are a total of** 12 Schedules** in the Indian Constitution.

 
 

 
 
Schedules

 
 
 
**Provision**

 
 
 

 
 
First Schedule

 
 
 
List of States & Union Territories

 
 
 

 
 
Second Schedule

 
 
 
Salary of President, Governors, Chief Judges, Judges of High Court and Supreme Court, Comptroller and Auditor General.

 
 
 

 
 
Third Schedule

 
 
 
Forms of Oaths and affirmations

 
 
 

 
 
Fourth Schedule

 
 
 
Allocate seats for each state of India in Rajya Sabha

 
 
 

 
 
Fifth Schedule

 
 
 
Administration and control of scheduled areas and tribes.

 
 
 

 
 
Sixth Schedule

 
 
 
Provisions for the administration of Tribal Area in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram & Arunachal Pradesh

 
 
 

 
 
Seventh Schedule

 
 
 
Gives allocation of powers and functions between Union & States. It contains 3 lists Union List, States, Concurrent List

 
 
 

 
 
Eighth Schedule

 
 
 
List of 22 languages of India recognized by Constitution

 
 
 

 
 
Ninth Schedule

 
 
 
It contains acts & orders related to land tenure, land tax, railways, and industries.

 
 
 

 
 
Tenth Schedule

 
 
 
It contains provisions of disqualification on grounds of defection.

 
 
 

 
 
Eleventh Schedule

 
 
 
It contains provisions of Panchayati Raj.

 
 
 

 
 
Twelfth Schedule

 
 
 
It contains provisions of Municipal Corporation.

questions.question: "Neel Darpan" was written by Dinbandhu Mitra to portray the oppression faced by peasants to grow indigo in:
questions.solution:
**__Answer : (2)__ - Bengal** - Neel Darpan was a Bengali play written by Dinbandhu Mitra in 1858-59. The play was published in Dhaka in 1860.

 
• The play was essential to Nil Vidroha or Indigo revolt of February-March 1859 in Bengal when farmers refused to sow Indigo in their fields to protest against exploitative farming under British Raj.
 
• **Michael Madhusudan Dutt** translated this immemorable Bengali drama in English and published by Reverend James Long.
 
• The characters in the drama are the villagers and the indigo planters who have the money and the law in their hands.

questions.question: Who among the following takes part in election of the President of India?

options.text: Elected Members of both the houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of the states.
Elected and nominated members of both the houses of Parliament.
Elected and nominated members of both the houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of the states.
Elected members of both the houses of Parliament only.

questions.solution:
__**Answer: (1)**__ - **Elected Members of both the Houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of the states.**

 
• The President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both the Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and the Union Territories of Delhi and Pondicherry.
 
• **Article 52** of the Constitution of India deals with the office of President.
 
• The manner of election of President is provided by** Article 55** of the Constitution.
 
• The general principle of the election of President is that the total number of votes cast by Member of Parliament equals the total number of votes cast by state legislators.
 
• **Part 5** of the Constitution under Chapter-1 (The Executive) lists out the qualification, election, and impeachment of the President of India (Article 52-Article 62).

questions.question: Which of the following Indian rulers was defeated by Mahmud Ghazni in his ﬁrst attack in the year 1001 AD?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaya Pala.**__

**Jaya Pala **- was a famous ruler from** Hindushahi Dynasty,** which extended from Punjab to Kabul. He ruled the Hindu Shahi kingdom from 964 to 1001 CE.

 
• He was defeated by Mahmud of Ghazni (997-1030) in Ghazni's first attack in the year 1000 AD. Jayapapa also fought the famous battle of Peshawar in the year 1001 with Mahmud of Ghazni but was defeated.
 
• He was succeeded by his son **Maharaja Anandapal**.

• He was the father of Anandapal.
 
• He was defeated by Ghaznavid ruler, Mahmud of Ghazni in 1000-1001 AD.
 
 
 
 

 Sukhpala
 1007-1010 CE
 
 
 
• He was the ruler of Multan who was appointed by Mahmud Ghazni because he had embraced Islam.
 
• He was punished by Mahmud of Ghazni when he gave up Islam and started ruling as an independent ruler in 1008.
 
 
 
 

 Anand Pala
 1001-1010 CE
